title: The Wardrobe of Room 214
premise: Mirabel Zhou, a celebrated restaurant critic who lost the ability to taste after a betrayal she has never named, is clearing out her late mother's house in Room 214 of a fading seaside hotel when a radio plays an unrecorded song her brother wrote and died before singing again. The song pulls Mirabel into vivid, involuntary relivings of the family's final summer, forcing her to confront the 'stranger' in the old photographs — her mother, whose silence protected a secret that destroyed them all. As the house sale deadline looms and her editor demands a career-defining review she cannot honestly write, Mirabel must choose between loyalty to her brother's grudge and the truth that her mother's silence was itself an act of protection. She forgives the stranger, tastes a single spoonful of soup at last, and lets the house go — keeping only the song.
about_author: Hazel Oyelaran is a former line cook turned novelist who writes about appetite, memory, and the families we audition for our whole lives. She lives near a cold coast and still salts everything too early.

chapters.title: Tenant
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. We meet her reviewing a tasting menu she describes with flawless technique and total emptiness, then returning to Room 214 to sort her dead mother's belongings before Friday's closing. Emotional beat: numb competence masking grief; the reader learns she hasn't tasted anything in three years.

chapters.title: The Song That Was Never Sung
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A hotel radio crackles into a melody Mirabel knows intimately — her brother Theo wrote it the summer he disappeared from the family, never recorded, never performed. She freezes mid-box. Emotional beat: shock cracking open the sealed past; the song begins pulling her into memory.

chapters.title: Photographs of a Stranger
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, slipping into memory. Among the boxes: photographs of her mother laughing in ways Mirabel never witnessed, beside a man who isn't their father. The first full flashback arrives unbidden — the kitchen, the song being written. Emotional beat: disorientation and the first flicker of anger at the stranger in the pictures.

chapters.title: Salt Without Taste
chapters.summary: Alternating Mirabel present-day and Theo's remembered voice. Her editor pressures her for the review of the year; a young chef's restaurant awaits her verdict. In flashbacks, teenage Theo teaches Mirabel to taste deliberately. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth surfaces — she can't write honestly because honesty is what broke the family.

chapters.title: What Mother Kept
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She finds her mother's locked tin: letters revealing the stranger was her mother's brother, erased from the family after testifying against their father — justice pursued outside the law, at devastating cost. Emotional beat: the ground shifts; the villain of Mirabel's story may have been its only honest person.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Deadline
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with the estate lawyer as foil. The sale closes Friday; a developer wants everything gutted. Mirabel stalls, inventing delays, while the song keeps surfacing — each verse unlocking a deeper scene of the summer Theo left. Emotional beat: rising tension, compulsion, the sense of racing a clock both legal and emotional.

chapters.title: Verse Three
chapters.summary: Deep flashback chapter, largely Theo's perspective rendered through Mirabel's immersion. The night of the betrayal: Mirabel, loyal to her father, repeated something Theo told her in confidence; it reached the wrong ears and cost him everything. Emotional beat: guilt inverted — Mirabel realizes she was the stranger in Theo's photographs.

chapters.title: The Review I Cannot Write
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She sits in the young chef's restaurant, notebook blank, surrounded by dishes she cannot taste, while the sale papers wait unsigned in her bag. She drafts a review that lies, then burns it in the ashtray. Emotional beat: crisis of identity — critic without palate, daughter without verdict, tenant of her own life.

chapters.title: Room 214, Empty
chapters.summary: Climax. On closing day, the song plays one final time and takes Mirabel fully into the last night — where her mother, not Theo, made the choice to stay silent to protect Mirabel from what she'd done. Mirabel speaks forgiveness aloud to the empty room, signs nothing, and stops the sale by claiming the house herself. Emotional beat: catharsis, ownership at last.

chapters.title: A Single Spoonful
chapters.summary: Resolution, Mirabel's POV. Weeks later, in the half-gutted house she now owns, Mirabel cooks her mother's soup from a stained recipe card. One spoonful — salt, fat, grief, sweetness. She writes the true review, crediting the young chef, and hums the finished song aloud, finally adding the ending Theo never wrote. Emotional beat: quiet restoration; belonging claimed, truth chosen over loyalty.
